questions.question: In a liquid-liquid separation of Chapter 20 reaction products using dichloromethane (density 1.33 g/mL) and water (density 1.00 g/mL), which is the bottom layer?

options.label: A
options.text: The aqueous layer is always on the bottom regardless of solvent.

options.label: B
options.text: The layers mix completely and cannot separate.

options.label: C
options.text: The organic layer floats on top.

options.label: D
options.text: The dichloromethane (organic) layer is the bottom layer due to its higher density compared to water in Chapter 20.

questions.correct_answer: The dichloromethane (organic) layer is the bottom layer due to its higher density compared to water in Chapter 20.
questions.explanation: Halogenated solvents (CH₂Cl₂, CHCl₃) have densities > 1.0 g/mL and form the bottom layer in separatory funnels.

questions.topic: Ch20 Silica Gel Chromatography Polarity Order
questions.question: On a normal-phase silica column in Chapter 20, what is the elution order of hydrocarbons, ketones, and carboxylic acids?

options.label: A
options.text: Hydrocarbons (least polar, elute first) → Ketones (moderately polar) → Carboxylic acids (most polar, elute last) in Chapter 20.

options.label: B
options.text: Ketones elute first → Hydrocarbons → Carboxylic acids.

options.label: C
options.text: Carboxylic acids elute first → Ketones → Hydrocarbons.

options.label: D
options.text: All three compounds elute together.

questions.correct_answer: Hydrocarbons (least polar, elute first) → Ketones (moderately polar) → Carboxylic acids (most polar, elute last) in Chapter 20.
questions.explanation: Nonpolar compounds have the weakest affinity for polar silica gel and elute first; polar compounds elute last.

questions.question: Why does fractional distillation achieve superior separation over simple distillation for Chapter 20 liquid mixtures with close boiling points (Δbp < 25°C)?

options.label: A
options.text: The fractionating column provides multiple sequential condensation-vaporization cycles (theoretical plates), progressively enriching the rising vapor in the lower-boiling component in Chapter 20.

options.label: B
options.text: The column works only under high vacuum.

options.label: C
options.text: The column destroys the higher-boiling component.

options.label: D
options.text: The column heats the mixture to 1000°C.

questions.correct_answer: The fractionating column provides multiple sequential condensation-vaporization cycles (theoretical plates), progressively enriching the rising vapor in the lower-boiling component in Chapter 20.
questions.explanation: Fractionating columns increase internal surface area, allowing repeated micro-distillations that separate liquids with close boiling points.

options.label: D

questions.question: Which of the following solvents is classified as a 'preferred green solvent' for Chapter 20 laboratory protocols?

options.label: A
options.text: Carbon tetrachloride (CCl₄).

options.label: B
options.text: Benzene.

options.label: C
options.text: Ethanol, water, or 2-methyltetrahydrofuran (2-MeTHF), replacing toxic and non-renewable chlorinated solvents in Chapter 20.

options.label: D
options.text: Hexamethylphosphoramide (HMPA).

questions.correct_answer: Ethanol, water, or 2-methyltetrahydrofuran (2-MeTHF), replacing toxic and non-renewable chlorinated solvents in Chapter 20.

questions.question: If a Chapter 20 compound migrates 4.0 cm on a TLC plate while the solvent front travels 8.0 cm, what is its Retention Factor (Rf)?

options.label: D
options.text: Rf = 0.50 (Rf = distance traveled by compound / distance traveled by solvent front = 4.0 cm / 8.0 cm = 0.50) in Chapter 20.

questions.correct_answer: Rf = 0.50 (Rf = distance traveled by compound / distance traveled by solvent front = 4.0 cm / 8.0 cm = 0.50) in Chapter 20.
questions.explanation: The Retention Factor Rf is the ratio of solute migration distance to solvent front migration distance (0 ≤ Rf ≤ 1).

questions.question: If a supersaturated Chapter 20 solution fails to crystallize upon cooling, what physical laboratory technique induces crystal nucleation?

options.label: A
options.text: Freezing the solution into solid ice.

options.label: B
options.text: Boiling the solvent away completely with a torch.

options.label: C
options.text: Adding 1 liter of concentrated acid.

options.label: D
options.text: Scratching the inside glass wall with a glass stirring rod or adding a tiny 'seed crystal' of pure compound in Chapter 20.

questions.correct_answer: Scratching the inside glass wall with a glass stirring rod or adding a tiny 'seed crystal' of pure compound in Chapter 20.
questions.explanation: Scratching provides micro-glass particles as nucleation sites; seed crystals provide a pre-formed crystal lattice template.

questions.question: In gas chromatography analysis of Chapter 20 volatile compounds on a nonpolar capillary column, what factor primarily dictates retention time?

options.label: A
options.text: Molecular optical rotation.

options.label: B
options.text: pH of the carrier gas.

options.label: C
options.text: Color of the compound.

options.label: D
options.text: Boiling point: lower-boiling, more volatile compounds partition more into the carrier gas and elute first (shorter retention time) in Chapter 20.

questions.correct_answer: Boiling point: lower-boiling, more volatile compounds partition more into the carrier gas and elute first (shorter retention time) in Chapter 20.
questions.explanation: On nonpolar GC stationary phases, elution order is determined primarily by boiling point and vapor pressure.

questions.question: What is the standard, safe laboratory protocol for quenching excess sodium hydride (NaH) or lithium aluminum hydride (LiAlH₄) after a Chapter 20 reaction?

options.label: A
options.text: Slow, dropwise addition of isopropanol or ethyl acetate followed by water under an inert atmosphere with vigorous cooling in Chapter 20.

options.label: B
options.text: Heating with an open Bunsen burner.

options.label: C
options.text: Dumping the entire flask into pure water instantly.

options.label: D
options.text: Pouring concentrated nitric acid into the flask.

questions.correct_answer: Slow, dropwise addition of isopropanol or ethyl acetate followed by water under an inert atmosphere with vigorous cooling in Chapter 20.
questions.explanation: Hydrides react violently with water; cautious quenching with a mild protic alcohol (isopropanol) safely mitigates rapid hydrogen gas release.

options.text: E-Factor = 0.04.

questions.question: In a liquid-liquid separation of Chapter 20 reaction products using dichloromethane (density 1.33 g/mL) and water (density 1.00 g/mL), which is the bottom layer?

options.label: A
options.text: The organic layer floats on top.

options.label: B
options.text: The aqueous layer is always on the bottom regardless of solvent.

options.label: C
options.text: The dichloromethane (organic) layer is the bottom layer due to its higher density compared to water in Chapter 20.

options.label: D
options.text: The layers mix completely and cannot separate.

questions.correct_answer: The dichloromethane (organic) layer is the bottom layer due to its higher density compared to water in Chapter 20.
questions.explanation: Halogenated solvents (CH₂Cl₂, CHCl₃) have densities > 1.0 g/mL and form the bottom layer in separatory funnels.

questions.topic: Ch20 Silica Gel Chromatography Polarity Order
questions.question: On a normal-phase silica column in Chapter 20, what is the elution order of hydrocarbons, ketones, and carboxylic acids?

options.label: A
options.text: Ketones elute first → Hydrocarbons → Carboxylic acids.

options.label: B
options.text: All three compounds elute together.

options.label: C
options.text: Hydrocarbons (least polar, elute first) → Ketones (moderately polar) → Carboxylic acids (most polar, elute last) in Chapter 20.

options.label: D
options.text: Carboxylic acids elute first → Ketones → Hydrocarbons.

questions.correct_answer: Hydrocarbons (least polar, elute first) → Ketones (moderately polar) → Carboxylic acids (most polar, elute last) in Chapter 20.
questions.explanation: Nonpolar compounds have the weakest affinity for polar silica gel and elute first; polar compounds elute last.

questions.question: Why does fractional distillation achieve superior separation over simple distillation for Chapter 20 liquid mixtures with close boiling points (Δbp < 25°C)?

options.label: A
options.text: The column destroys the higher-boiling component.

options.label: B
options.text: The fractionating column provides multiple sequential condensation-vaporization cycles (theoretical plates), progressively enriching the rising vapor in the lower-boiling component in Chapter 20.

options.label: C
options.text: The column heats the mixture to 1000°C.

options.label: D
options.text: The column works only under high vacuum.

questions.correct_answer: The fractionating column provides multiple sequential condensation-vaporization cycles (theoretical plates), progressively enriching the rising vapor in the lower-boiling component in Chapter 20.
questions.explanation: Fractionating columns increase internal surface area, allowing repeated micro-distillations that separate liquids with close boiling points.

questions.correct_answer: 100% Atom Economy, representing maximum sustainability with zero chemical byproduct generation in Chapter 20.
questions.explanation: Addition and pericyclic reactions incorporate all reactant atoms into the product, achieving ideal 100% atom economy.

options.text: Rf = 0.50 (Rf = distance traveled by compound / distance traveled by solvent front = 4.0 cm / 8.0 cm = 0.50) in Chapter 20.

questions.question: If a supersaturated Chapter 20 solution fails to crystallize upon cooling, what physical laboratory technique induces crystal nucleation?

questions.explanation: On nonpolar GC stationary phases, elution order is determined primarily by boiling point and vapor pressure.
